title: Prove It: 4s and 6s
goal: I can solve 4s and 6s facts, find a missing number, and pick the right operation.

card.desc: Prove it day for Week 2. Bristol mixes 4s and 6s facts, finds a missing number (4 × ? = 24) by counting jumps or by guess and check, and reads word problems where the same two numbers can mean multiply or add. The check is the strongest of the week.

win: You proved it! 4s and 6s are yours!

slides.title: On Your Own: Prove It
slides.text: You proved it in class. Now prove it on your own. 💪

slides.title: Think about your book
slides.text: Read each question. Tell a grown-up your answer.
prompts: What was your favorite part this week? Why?
What question would you ask Amy?

items.why: Turn-around facts have the same answer: 7 × 3 = 21.
items.no: Turn it around. The answer does not change.

items.q: There are 4 tanks. Each tank has 6 fish. How many fish?
items.why: 4 equal groups of 6. Double 6 is 12. Double 12 is 24.

slides.title: Find the hiding number
slides.tip: Count the jumps, not the last number.

items.no: Count by 4s to 12. How many jumps?
Count by 6s to 30. How many jumps?

items.why: Turn it around: 4 × 3. Double 3 is 6. Double 6 is 12.
Turn it around: 6 × 8. 5 × 8 = 40, plus one more 8 is 48.
no: Double, double is for 4s. This fact has a 6.
8 + 6 adds. 8 × 6 is 8 groups of 6.

slides.title: Multiply or add?
slides.text: Same numbers! Read the words. Tap a card. Then tap the right box.

items.text: Liz has 6 jars. Each jar has 4 bugs.
Liz has 6 red jars and 4 blue jars.
items.why: 6 red and 4 blue are not equal groups: 6 + 4 = 10.

items.text: There are 4 teams with 6 kids on every team.
Amy ran 4 laps. Then she ran 6 more laps.
Marion buys 6 packs. There are 4 pens per pack.
Ellie has 6 big dogs and 4 small dogs.
items.hint: Does she have the same number of each?

slides.done: Same numbers, different job. The words decide!

items.q: Liz has 18 bones. She puts 6 bones in each bowl. How many bowls?
items.no: How many 6s make 18? Count the jumps.

items.q: There are 6 vases. Each vase has 9 tulips. How many tulips?
items.no: Each vase has 9. Use your 5s, then one more group.

items.q: Amy has 9 tulips. Ellie has 6 tulips. How many tulips in all?
items.why: 9 and 6 are not equal groups. Add: 9 + 6 = 15.
items.no: Is there a clue word? Are the groups the same size?

slides.title: Crayon boxes
slides.text: Marion has 4 boxes. Every box has 9 crayons. Make the groups.
slides.why: 4 groups of 9. Double 9 is 18. Double 18 is 36.
slides.hint: Each box is one group. Groups = how many boxes. In each group = crayons in one box.

items.q: Mia says the hiding number in 6 × ? = 42 is 36. She did 42 − 6. What is the hiding number?
items.no: How many 6s make 42? Count the jumps or guess, check and fix.

no: 12 is 4 + 8. Multiply.
28 is 4 × 7. Double, double for 4 × 8.

sets.why: 7 rows of 6 is the same as 6 × 7. 35 + 7 = 42.

sets.no: How many 4s make 28? Count the jumps.

no: 42 is 48 − 6. The hiding number is how many 6s.
6 × 9 = 54. Too big.

sets.why: Turn it around: 4 × 8. Double 8 is 16. Double 16 is 32.

sets.q: There are 6 kennels. Every kennel has 6 puppies. How many puppies?
sets.no: Every kennel has 6. Use your 5s, then one more group.

sets.q: Liz walked 4 big dogs and 7 small dogs. How many dogs did she walk?
sets.why: 4 and 7 are not equal groups. Add: 4 + 7 = 11.
no: 4 and 7 are not equal groups. Add.
3 is the difference. The question asks how many dogs.

sets.q: Amy put 24 treats in bags. Each bag has 4 treats. How many bags?
sets.no: How many 4s make 24? Count the jumps.

no: 45 + 9 is 6 × 9. This fact has a 4.
4 + 9 adds. 4 × 9 is 4 groups of 9.

sets.why: Turn it around: 4 × 7. Double 7 is 14. Double 14 is 28.

sets.no: How many 6s make 24? Count the jumps.

no: 32 is 36 − 4. The hiding number is how many 4s.
4 × 8 = 32. Too small.

sets.no: Cover the last row. 5 rows of 9 is 45.

sets.q: There are 6 boats. Every boat has 7 kids. How many kids?
sets.no: Every boat has 7. Use your 5s, then one more group.

sets.q: Ellie read 6 pages. Then she read 8 more pages. How many pages?
sets.why: 6 and 8 are not equal groups. Add: 6 + 8 = 14.
no: 48 is 6 × 8. These are not equal groups. Add.
2 is the difference. The question asks how many pages.

sets.q: Marion has 36 beads. She puts 6 on each string. How many strings?
sets.no: How many 6s make 36? Guess, check and fix.

no: Double, double is for 4s. That makes 4 × 8.
The extra group has 8, not 6.

sets.why: 8 rows of 6 is the same as 6 × 8. 40 + 8 = 48.

sets.no: How many 4s make 40? Count the jumps.

no: 54 is 60 − 6. The hiding number is how many 6s.
6 × 9 = 54. Too small.

sets.why: 4 groups of 9. Double 9 is 18. Double 18 is 36.

sets.q: There are 4 shelves. Each shelf has 8 books. How many books?
sets.why: 4 equal groups of 8. Double 8 is 16. Double 16 is 32.

sets.q: Amy has 9 pens. Liz has 4 pens. How many pens in all?
sets.why: 9 and 4 are not equal groups. Add: 9 + 4 = 13.
no: 36 is 9 × 4. These are not equal groups. Add.
5 is the difference. The question asks how many pens.

sets.q: Ellie has 42 stickers. She puts 6 on each page. How many pages?
sets.no: How many 6s make 42? Guess, check and fix.

sets.q: Theo says 6 × 6 = 35. What did he do?
choices: He added one more 5, not one more 6.
sets.why: 5 × 6 = 30. He added 5. He needed one more 6: 30 + 6 = 36.
no: Doubling two times is for 4s. Theo used 5 × 6 = 30, then added 5.

practice.intro: Three tries on each one. Only your first try counts. 4s: double, double. 6s: 5s + one more. Hiding number: count the jumps.

questions.why: Turn it around: 4 × 10. Double 10 is 20. Double 20 is 40.

questions.no: Count by 4s to 16. How many jumps?

no: 30 is 36 − 6. How many 6s make 36?
6 × 7 = 42. Too big.

questions.no: How many 4s make 32? Guess, check and fix.

questions.q: How many apples? Turn it around!
questions.why: 9 rows of 6 is the same as 6 × 9. 45 + 9 = 54.
questions.no: 9 × 6 is the same as 6 × 9. Start with 5 × 9.

questions.q: There are 4 benches. 7 kids sit on each bench. How many kids?
Marion has 6 red beads and 9 blue beads. How many beads?
no: There are not 6 groups of 9. Add.
3 is the difference. The question asks how many beads.

questions.q: Liz has 60 seeds. She plants 6 in every pot. How many pots?
questions.no: How many 6s make 60? Guess, check and fix.

choices: There are 6 bowls with 4 fish in each.
no: 4 dogs and 6 cats are different groups. Add.
6 pages and 4 pages are different. Add.
That is 17. You need 5 groups of 4 plus one more 4.
6 + 4 adds. 6 × 4 is 6 groups of 4.

pages.title: Part 1: Fact check
pages.directions: Write the answer. 4s: double, double. 6s: 5s + one more.

pages.title: Part 2: Find the hiding number
pages.directions: Count the jumps, or guess, check and fix.

pages.title: Part 3: Fix it
pages.directions: Each fact is wrong. Write the right answer.

pages.title: Part 4: Draw it
pages.directions: Draw a picture. Then write the number sentence.

items.text: 13. Liz has 24 dog biscuits. She puts 6 in each bag. How many bags?
14. Marion has 4 bags. Every bag has 6 marbles. How many marbles?
15. Ellie found 4 shells. Liz found 6 shells. How many shells?
16. There are 6 dogs. Every dog gets 9 treats. How many treats?

pages.title: Part 6: Book corner
pages.directions: Tell the story so far in order. Use First, Next and Then. Use capital letters and periods.

teacher.objective: Bristol proves the Week 2 facts: mixed 4s (double, double) and 6s (5s + one more group), including turn-arounds; finds a missing factor (4 × ? = 24) by counting jumps or by guess, check and fix; and chooses multiply or add when two stories use the same numbers.
materials: Index cards: write 8 facts (4 × 6, 6 × 6, 6 × 8, 4 × 9, 6 × 4, 8 × 6, 4 × 7, 6 × 7) for a quick flash round
Her book, Amy and the Missing Puppy
Printed Lesson 5 packet to send home if you can (her task list also tells her to print it)

plan.do: Class slides 1–2. She retells in order (her strength), then the harder prompts: most important clue, and how Amy has changed.
Class slides 3–4. Index cards: trick, then answer. Keep an "again" pile. Then the pick-the-trick review.
Class slides 5–8. Number line for 4 × ? = 24 (count the jumps). 30 beans into cups of 6 (5 cups). Guess, check and fix for 6 × ? = 42, saying "too small" or "too big". Then three on her own.
Class slide 9 (sort). 4 × 9 and 6 × 6 are both 36: the answer alone does not tell you the fact.
Class slides 10–12. Build Story A (cups) and Story B (two piles). Word problems: she points to each/every or says it is missing. She builds 6 bowls of 8.

plan.block: Story hiding number and Fix it
plan.do: Class slides 13–14. Act out 28 stickers, 4 per page, with beans. She explains Theo's and Mia's mistakes in her own words.
Class slide 15. Hiding numbers and a multiply/add pair with the same numbers, written on the whiteboard before you click.
Class slide 16. Repeat the "again" flash cards. Read the weekend task list together, including Times Table Trail Lesson 3.

watch: Answering with the product instead of the hiding number (4 × ? = 24 → "24"). Ask: "How many jumps?"
Subtracting to find a hiding number (32 − 4 = 28). Have her check: does 4 × 28 make 32?
Multiplying any 4 and 6 she sees (Amy's 6 toys and Ellie's 4 toys = 24). Make her find the word each or every first.
The story hiding-number items on the check (for example 24 treats, 4 in each bag) need the hiding number, not the total. If she adds or subtracts, act it out with beans and cups.

packet_key.answer: 24 (Mia doubled only once: double 6 is 12, double 12 is 24)
4 bags. Picture: 24 biscuits in bags of 6 (4 bags). 6 × 4 = 24 (or 6 × ? = 24, ? = 4)
Three events from the book in the right order, each a complete sentence with a capital letter and a period.

teacher.notes: Show What You Know is at the end of the after-class lesson; she needs 85 (7 of 8) to open Lesson 6, and a retake gives her a brand-new set of 8. If she is still under 85 by Monday, open the Zoom lesson (Lesson 6) with 8 minutes on the missed type: hiding numbers with beans and cups at home, or the each/every routine for word problems. Do not start ×8 until 4 × 6, 4 × 7, 4 × 8 and 4 × 9 are quick, because ×8 is built on the 4s.

slides.title: Prove It: 4s and 6s
slides.text: This week you learned two tricks. Today you prove you can use them. 💪

notes.do: Set out: about 50 beans, 6 small cups, the 8 flash cards (4 × 6, 6 × 6, 6 × 8, 4 × 9, 6 × 4, 8 × 6, 4 × 7, 6 × 7), whiteboard and marker, her book.
notes.say: This week you learned two tricks. Today you prove you can use them, find a hiding number, and pick the right operation.
notes.listen: "4s: double, double. 6s: 5s plus one more group."

slides.title: Tell it in order
slides.text: Think about Amy and the Missing Puppy.
prompts: Tell the story so far. What happened first, next, then?
What is the most important clue so far? Why?
How has Amy changed since the start?
starters: At the start Amy … Now she …

notes.do: 5–6 minutes. Retelling in order is her strength; let her lead, then push on the harder prompts.
notes.ask: Tell the story so far in order. What is the most important clue, and why? How has Amy changed?
notes.listen: First, next, then with real events; a clue with a reason; a change from the start (worried → hopeful, or alone → with friends).

slides.title: Flash round
slides.text: Your teacher shows a card. Say the trick, then the answer.

notes.do: Show each index card. She says the trick first, then the answer. Put any card she has to think hard about in a "again" pile and repeat those at the end.
notes.listen: 24, 36, 48, 36, 24, 48, 28, 42. For 8 × 6 she should turn it around to 6 × 8.

no: 12 + 12 is double, double. That is 4 × 6 = 24.
Add one more group of 6, not 1.
45 + 9 is 6 × 9. This fact is 4 × 9.
27 is 18 + 9. That is not a double.

items.q: How many stars? 8 rows of 4. Turn it around!
items.why: 8 × 4 is the same as 4 × 8. Double 8 is 16. Double 16 is 32.

notes.listen: "12 + 12 is double, double. That is for 4s." 32 for the stars.

slides.title: A number is hiding!

steps.text: Count by 4s to 24. Each jump is 4.
Now count the jumps: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. There are 6 jumps.
So 4 × 6 = 24. The hiding number is 6.

slides.tip: Count the jumps, not the last number. 24 is where you land. 6 is how many jumps.

notes.do: Click one step at a time. She counts the jumps on her fingers.
notes.say: When a number is hiding, count how many 4s it takes to reach 24.
notes.ask: Where do we land? How many jumps did it take?
notes.listen: "We land on 24. It took 6 jumps." If she says 24 is the answer, point back to the question mark: it stands for the number of jumps.

slides.title: Fill the cups
slides.text: You have 30 beans. Put 6 in each cup. How many cups do you fill?

steps.text: Fill one cup with 6. Then another. Keep going until the beans are gone.
You filled 5 cups.
So 6 × 5 = 30. The hiding number is 5.

slides.tip: The hiding number is how many groups.

notes.do: Count out exactly 30 beans with her. She fills cups of 6 until the beans run out.
notes.ask: How many cups? Write the fact with the hiding number.

slides.title: Guess, check, fix
slides.text: 6 × ? = 42. Try a number. Check it. Fix it.

steps.text: Guess 6. 6 × 6 = 36. That is too small.
So 6 × 7 = 42. The hiding number is 7.

slides.tip: Too small? Try a bigger number. Too big? Try a smaller number.

notes.do: She says each guess out loud and "too small" or "too big" before you click.
notes.ask: 6 × 6 is 36. Is 42 more or less? So should the next guess be bigger or smaller?

items.no: How many 4s make 32? Count the jumps.
items.hint: Count by 4s: 4, 8, 12 … until you land on 32. Count the jumps.

items.no: Count by 6s to 18. How many jumps?

no: 6 × 8 = 48. Too small. Try one more.
48 is 54 − 6. The hiding number is how many 6s.

notes.do: She can use beans and cups or count jumps on her fingers.
notes.listen: 8, 3, 9. If she types 28 or 12, she subtracted: ask, "Does 4 × 28 make 32?"

slides.title: Same answer, same box
slides.text: Tap a fact. Then tap the box with its answer.

notes.do: She says the answer and the trick before she taps each card.
notes.say: Look at the 36 box: 4 × 9 and 6 × 6. The answer alone does not tell you the fact.
notes.listen: She notices that two different facts can have the same answer.

slides.title: Same numbers, different job
slides.text: Both stories have a 4 and a 6. Read carefully!

steps.text: Story A: There are 4 puppies. Each puppy has 6 spots. How many spots?
Each puppy has 6. Equal groups. Multiply: 4 × 6 = 24 spots.
Story B: Amy has 4 puppies. Ellie has 6 puppies. How many puppies?
4 and 6 are not the same. Add: 4 + 6 = 10 puppies.

slides.tip: Don't look only at the numbers. Look for each or every. Ask: are the groups equal?

notes.do: Build Story A with 4 cups of 6 beans, and Story B with a pile of 4 and a pile of 6.
notes.say: Same numbers. Different job. The words decide, not the numbers.
notes.ask: Which story has the clue word? Which one adds?
notes.listen: "Story A says each, so multiply. Story B has no clue word and the groups are different, so add."

slides.title: Word problems
slides.text: Equal groups? Multiply. Not equal? Add.

items.q: Six friends each brought 4 apples to the picnic. How many apples?
items.no: Each friend brought 4. That is 6 equal groups.

items.q: Amy has 6 dog toys. Ellie has 4 cat toys. How many toys?
items.why: 6 and 4 are two different groups. Add: 6 + 4 = 10.
no: Amy does not have 6 groups of 4. Add the two amounts.
2 is the difference. The question asks how many toys.

items.q: The vet has 4 cages. There are 9 birds in every cage. How many birds?
items.why: Every cage has 9. Double 9 is 18, double 18 is 36.

notes.do: Before answering she points to each or every, or says it is missing.

slides.title: Snack bowls
slides.text: Amy fills 6 bowls. She puts 8 treats in every bowl. Make the groups.
slides.hint: Each bowl is one group. Groups = how many bowls. In each group = treats in one bowl.

notes.do: She builds 6 cups of 8 beans first, then sets the buttons.

slides.title: A hiding number in a story
slides.text: Liz has 28 stickers. She puts 4 on each page. How many pages?

steps.text: What do we know? 4 on each page. 28 in all.
Write it: 4 × ? = 28. The hiding number is the pages.
Count by 4s to 28. Count the jumps.
7 jumps. So 4 × 7 = 28. Liz fills 7 pages.

slides.tip: The total is in the story. The hiding number is how many groups.

notes.do: Act it out: 28 beans, 4 on each sheet of paper (or in each cup) until they run out.
notes.ask: Is 28 the answer? What does the question ask for?
notes.listen: "No, 28 is all the stickers. It asks how many pages: 7." If she adds 28 + 4 or multiplies 28 × 4, go back to the beans.

items.q: Theo says 6 × 6 = 31. He did 5 × 6 = 30, then 30 + 1. What should he do?
no: The extra group has 6, not 5.
He added 1. He needs one more group of 6.

notes.ask: Tell me in your own words what Theo did wrong. What did Mia forget?
notes.listen: "Theo added 1 instead of a group of 6." "Mia only doubled once."

slides.title: Prove it on the board
slides.text: Write each one on the whiteboard. Then check.

steps.text: Get your whiteboard and marker. Listen for the first one.
Liz has 6 bags with 7 marbles in each. → 6 × 7 = 42
Amy has 6 marbles. Ellie has 7 marbles. → 6 + 7 = 13

slides.tip: Hiding number: count the jumps. Story: look for each or every.

notes.do: Read each one aloud. She writes her answer and the fact on the whiteboard, then you click to check.
notes.listen: The last two use the same numbers: one multiplies, one adds. This is the skill the whole first two weeks built.

slides.title: You proved it!
slides.text: 4s and 6s are yours. You can find a hiding number too!
slides.tip: This weekend: check your list. It has the after-class lesson, practice, packets, reading and Times Table Trail.

notes.do: Repeat any flash cards from the "again" pile. Then open the course page and read the Lesson 5 task list together.
notes.say: Next week: 7s, 8s and 9s. The 8s are built on your 4s, so keep doubling.
notes.ask: How do you find a hiding number?
notes.listen: "Count the jumps" or "guess, check and fix."
